releases.name: Anka Native 0.3.0
releases.body:
Anka Native 0.3.0 draws the tree canopies, plants and the arch beside Link's door that 0.2.2 left out, adds a 3D resolution setting, a faster Prepare on the phone and three new languages.
It is still slow: Kokiri Forest runs at about 14 fps on our test phone, and frames are slower than in 0.2.2 where the new content is on screen. The change for the Adreno 840 hang (#5) is untested because we have no Adreno 840.

"Tested on the phone" below means our only test phone: POCO F8 Pro (Adreno 830, 12 GB, Android 16 / HyperOS). "Tests only" means automated tests or a computer, not a phone.

### What is new

- **Mesh-drawn content is now drawn.** Kokiri Forest's tree canopies, grass, ferns, flowers and the arch beside Link's door, and the Deku Tree upper floor's floor that was invisible ([#6](https://github.com/EddizEge/AnkaNative/issues/6)). 0.2.2 skipped these draws on Turnip drivers. Your pack gets the needed shaders through an automatic update (see *After updating*). Tested on the phone with Anka Turnip: no draws skipped in Kokiri Forest and the Deku Tree's upper floor. Not tested on an Adreno 7xx, and not with Qualcomm's own driver.

releases.name: Anka Native 0.2.2
releases.body:
### Security fix

- **The launcher no longer takes control commands from other apps** ([#7](https://github.com/EddizEge/AnkaNative/issues/7)).
  - Before this release, any app on the phone could ask Anka Native's launcher to install or pick a GPU driver, add a game, start Prepare, or export or import a pack. These are commands meant for testing over adb.
  - The app now ignores them and shows a short message, unless you turn on **Settings › ADB control (debug)**. That switch is off by default and asks before it turns on. Turn it on only while you use adb.
  - Starting a game from a frontend works as before.

Everything else is as in [0.2.1](https://github.com/EddizEge/AnkaNative/releases/tag/v0.2.1). The full list of changes is in [CHANGELOG_ANKA_NATIVE.md](https://github.com/EddizEge/AnkaNative/blob/main/CHANGELOG_ANKA_NATIVE.md).

### Files

- `anka-native-0.2.2.apk`: the app (`dev.ankanative.android`), signed with the release key. Certificate SHA-256: `4d7443354f53a0aef11bc4df1a34ff3fc5bd6d748bbeb76fd78c80a6841f3bb0`. It installs over earlier versions and keeps your saves.

releases.name: Anka Native 0.2.1
releases.body:
### Fixes

- **Prepare on the phone stopped at the end for Ocarina of Time** ([#3](https://github.com/EddizEge/AnkaNative/issues/3)): "76 of 42346 shaders did not build: no library written".

  The same 76 shaders don't build on a computer either, and the game runs without them. Ocarina of Time's profile was missing the list that tells the phone which shaders those are, so the phone counted them as failures. 0.2.1 adds the list.

  Checked on a computer with the phone's rule: the library is now written, byte for byte the one a computer makes.

  **If your Prepare stopped with this message:** update to 0.2.1, open the game's card and tap **Retry**. The shaders already translated are kept, so it only tries the 76 again and then writes the library.

### New

- **Prepare on a computer on Windows** too, besides Linux and the Mac. Setup: [android/README.md](https://github.com/EddizEge/AnkaNative/blob/main/android/README.md#the-environment).
- **[Discussions](https://github.com/EddizEge/AnkaNative/discussions)** are open. Tell us how it runs on your phone in the [device reports](https://github.com/EddizEge/AnkaNative/discussions/1) thread.

releases.name: Anka Native 0.2.0
releases.body:
**Prepare on the phone (experimental).** The app can now make a game's pack from your dump on the phone itself. You no longer need a computer.

### How

Copy your dump (or `.nup`) to the phone, open **Anka Native**, tap **Add game**, pick the dump and tap **Prepare**. The app does three things in the background, with a notification:

1. It rewrites the game's code.
2. It scans the game's files for shaders.
3. It translates the shaders.

When it is done, the game's card says Ready.

- **Keep the phone on a charger.** For Ocarina of Time, preparing takes about 3 hours and uses the CPU fully.
- If a step fails, the card says why. Its log is in `<title ID>-work/ondevice/logs` next to the dump. Preparing on a computer still works as before.

### What was tested

On a POCO F8 Pro with Ocarina of Time:

- **Code rewrite:** worked, about 3 minutes.
- **Shader scan:** worked, about 35 minutes for the game's 186,583 files. It found 42,346 shaders, as many as on a computer.

releases.name: Anka Native 0.1.1
releases.body:
A fix for 0.1.0: **Prepare on the phone looked done but made nothing to play.**

0.1.0 was built without the on-phone packer. Its Prepare ran a simulated engine: the progress finished, but the pack it made was an empty placeholder with no game code and no shaders, so Play could not start the game.

### What changed

- Without the on-phone packer, the app no longer offers Prepare. Home and the game's card now say to prepare the game on a computer (the README's [Install](https://github.com/EddizEge/AnkaNative#install) steps) and to pick that pack.
- A placeholder pack left by 0.1.0 is no longer shown as ready: the card says "No pack", and Play explains why.

Preparing on the phone itself is being worked on for a later release.

Everything else is as in [0.1.0](https://github.com/EddizEge/AnkaNative/releases/tag/v0.1.0): your own dump is needed, the driver is [Anka Turnip 1.0.0](https://github.com/EddizEge/AnkaTurnip/releases/tag/v1.0.0), and the RAM saver is recommended below 16 GB of RAM. Tested only on a POCO F8 Pro with Ocarina of Time.

releases.name: FF7Recomp 1.1.62
releases.body:
**Fixed: crashes in some scenes with Echo-S voices and ChaOS's Resized Models (#91)**

Reported in issue #91: with Echo-S 7's voices on, the game closed in some scenes, for example on boarding the Highwind from the world map.

Two mods were each changing half of the same scene. ChaOS's **BETA: Resized Models** option replaces the list of character models for 693 scenes, a list made to match the original game's scene scripts. Echo-S's voiced version brings its own scene scripts, and in 39 scenes those use more characters than ChaOS's list loads. In the Highwind's deck, for example, the scripts use 14 models and ChaOS's list has 10. The game then tried to animate a character that was never loaded and crashed on the first frame. (ChaOS's own description of the option warns that it can crash with gameplay mods.)

Now, when a mod's model list doesn't match the models the scene's scripts use, that list is left out for that scene, and the scene keeps the models that came with its own file. In those 39 scenes the characters have their normal size instead of ChaOS's resized one; everywhere else Resized Models works as before. The log (`ff7.log`) names each scene where this happens.

releases.name: v1.1.61
releases.body:
**Fixed: rare crashes at scene changes with sound-effect mods on (#90)**

Reported in issue #90: once in a while the game closed when entering a battle, leaving the menu, or moving between areas, more often with many mods on and little free memory. The crash records all showed the same thing: some other part of the app had a pointer whose lower half had been overwritten with zeros earlier on.

We tracked it down with a special memory-checking build on our test device, which caught it within a minute. The cause was in FFNx's sound-effect code, which is active whenever a mod replaces the game's sound effects (Echo-S, the Tsunamods set and others). It keeps one record per sound channel. Some calls used the wrong channel number, and every battle transition touched a channel that had no record. Each time, the game wrote a few bytes just past the end of that table, usually zeros, into memory that belonged to something else. Most of the time nothing happened; sometimes it hit a pointer, and whatever used that pointer next crashed.

releases.name: v1.1.60
releases.body:
**Fixed: the game could close a while after loading a save state from an earlier session (#91)**

Reported in issue #91 with Echo-S 7 voices on. The game keeps one data file open the whole time it runs: the sound archive it loads its own sound effects from. A save state stores the game's memory, and that memory held the open file's handle as it was in the session where the state was made. After you closed the game and loaded the state in a later session, that handle no longer pointed at anything. The next time a scene needed a sound the game hadn't loaded yet, the game crashed.

Whether you hit this depended on luck. It was more likely with mods that open many files, like Echo-S voices.

Save states now record which files the game has open, and opening them again is part of loading a state. States made with older versions are covered too: the sound archive is opened again when they load.

### Updating
Go to **Settings → Updates** in the launcher (or install this APK over your current version), then press **Play**. It asks to **Update the game** once (a few seconds).

APK SHA-256: `f29167fd9f2e8d88814386aacf28742669a42cc58810be4dca13f5972d3dd3ab`

releases.name: v1.1.59
releases.body:
**New: the launcher says what kind of device runs the game best, and what helps after a crash**

Suggested in issue #90. Rare crashes when a battle or scene is drawn for the first time are most often the phone running low on memory while the graphics driver prepares that scene's shaders. That is a hardware limit more than a bug, so the launcher now says so where you'll see it:

- **After the game crashes** (or Android closes it for memory), the launcher shows a short note once: what most often causes it, what helps, and a button to **Report a problem** if it keeps happening.
- **Report a problem** and **Game files** (first setup) show the recommendation.
- **Settings → Renderer** now recommends **OpenGL ES** on Mali GPUs (most MediaTek and Exynos phones).
- The README has the same line under *Playing*.

The recommendation: **8 GB of RAM or more, with other apps (browser tabs too) closed while you play.** Heavy mod sets need the most memory, above all on Vulkan. On Mali GPUs, OpenGL ES is usually the steadier choice.

![The note the launcher shows once after the game crashed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bhuiyah/ff7-recomp-android/main/docs/release-images/1.1.59-crash-tip.jpg)

releases.name: v1.1.58
releases.body:
**Fixed: the graphics-driver crash protection from 1.1.57 now covers OpenGL ES too**

1.1.57 started keeping the game's finished GPU programs on your device when you play on Vulkan, so the graphics driver doesn't have to compile them again on every launch (that compiler is where the crash in issue #90 happened). Many players use OpenGL ES instead, because Vulkan is slower on their phone, so the same now happens there: once the game has drawn something on OpenGL ES, later launches load the finished program instead of compiling it again.

If your driver ever refuses one of the kept programs (for example after a driver update), the game simply builds it again the normal way. As before, the first time you reach a scene still has to compile it, so this makes the crash less likely rather than impossible.

### Updating
Go to **Settings → Updates** in the launcher (or install this APK over your current version), then press **Play**. It asks to **Update the game** once (a few seconds).

APK SHA-256: `c43ba98db8402e5e569e0e26ae1f235e76ff0f739de33d7ba8ae1ed8c6f12909`
Signing certificate SHA-256: `4f:c0:18:09:12:1b:af:25:f5:8c:8f:5e:7a:47:c4:80:c4:f8:6c:1e:a0:66:6e:37:c7:41:19:13:40:4d:1d:7c`

releases.body:
You need **Xbox360 Call of Duty 3 (USA, Europe).iso** file for install!

> **Still in development: bugs can and will occur.**
> *Még fejlesztés alatt: hibák előfordulhatnak.*

The first release since [0.4.0](https://github.com/FrankHUN88453/CoD3Recomp/releases/tag/v0.4.0): one executable that keeps itself up to date, the game's own menus played with the mouse, prompts that name your keys, and a faster renderer.

## New

- **One file: `CoD3SP_s.exe`.** FFmpeg's libraries for the sound and the films are built into it; nothing else to unpack.
- **Updates itself.** At every start it asks GitHub for a newer release; if there is one, it downloads it, replaces itself and starts the new version. Turn it off with `auto_update = 0` under `[game]` in `CoD3Recomp.ini`, or start it with `--no-update`.
- **New first start.** The console window asks whether this is a fresh install (choose your disc image, then the folder to install into) or the game is already installed (choose the game's main folder, the one with `default.xex`).

releases.name: Call of Duty 3 - PC Port - 0.4.0
releases.body:
You need **Xbox360 Call of Duty 3 (USA, Europe).iso** file for install!

> **Still in development: bugs can and will occur.**
> *Még fejlesztés alatt: hibák előfordulhatnak.*

The first release since [0.3.0](https://github.com/FrankHUN88453/CoD3Recomp/releases/tag/v0.3.0): a faster game, a picture closer to the console's, and two experimental options that make it faster still.

## New

- **Faster on every level.** The emulated kernel woke every waiting thread whenever anything was signalled (one of the game's locks is released some 50,000 times a second); now only the threads waiting for that object wake. The game's CPU use dropped from about 5.4 cores to 3.3, and the forest at 1080p without MSAA went from about 91 to 95–108 frames a second.
- **Native command lists (experimental)**, in the F11 menu, after a restart. The draws are made from the game's own Direct3D calls, and the console's GPU command stream is run only for what the GPU still has to do. With **Watch memory writes (experimental)** also on, the forest at 1080p without MSAA runs at about 180 frames a second. Tested on eight levels, the films and mission restarts; off by default until it has been played more.

## New

- **The next mission after a win.** The console restarts the game between missions and hands the next one over; the port does the same, so a finished mission leads into the next one instead of closing the game.
- **A mission's briefing film can be skipped** with Space (A) once its level has loaded. On the console it always plays to its end.
- **Unlimited frame rate in levels** (settings menu, on by default). A level runs at what the machine can do, around 100 to 115 frames a second where it had 60; the menus stay at 60 and the films at their own 30. The game's speed does not change with the frame rate.

releases.name: Call of Duty 3 - PC Port - 0.2.3
releases.body:
You need **Xbox360 Call of Duty 3 (USA, Europe).iso** file for install!

A fix release over [0.2.2](https://github.com/FrankHUN88453/CoD3Recomp/releases/tag/v0.2.2), and the one worth updating for: the lighting is right now.

## Fixed

**Walls lit far too brightly, and the odd shading on the soldiers and on the player's hands.** An instruction of the console's shaders has a vector half and a scalar half, and they run together: both read the registers as they were before the instruction and only then write. The translation wrote the vector's result first, so a scalar that read the very register the vector wrote got the new value instead of the old one.

The game's third light per surface is written exactly that way. Its scalar wants the specular exponent times a logarithm; with the write first it took a dot product instead, and two to the tenth of that became the specular. Every lit stone wall in Mayenne came out white with pink and green speckle, and characters were shaded oddly for the same reason. Eighty of the six hundred shader programs a level draws with have such an instruction, so this shows up all over the game, not only on that wall.

## Known issues

releases.name: Call of Duty 3 - PC Port - 0.2.2
releases.body:
You need **Xbox360 Call of Duty 3 (USA, Europe).iso** file for install!

A fix release over [0.2.1](https://github.com/FrankHUN88453/CoD3Recomp/releases/tag/v0.2.1); everything below is on top of what 0.2.1 brought.

## Fixed

**The HUD and the menu still flickered.** 0.2.1 looked at every texture every frame again, but a large one that had been still for a while was only *sampled*: sixty four places out of it. The HUD's fonts, icons and compass are small and change a handful of texels at a time, and the samples missed those changes, so the old picture stayed up for a frame. Everything up to two megabytes is now hashed whole, every frame, and only what is bigger than that falls back to sampling.

**Shadow filtering collapsed.** A texture fetch on the console carries three signed offsets in halves of a texel. The game's shadows are one map fetched four times at the corners of a texel; with the offsets dropped those were four fetches of the same texel, so a surface came out wholly lit or wholly dark instead of softly edged.

new update fellas:D this one brings more optimization and bug fixes

Mobile Odyssey 0.4 (beta)

There are two APKs. odyssey-0.4.apk is for most phones (ARMv8.2 or newer). odyssey-0.4-armv8.0.apk is for phones with older processors (ARMv8.0 or 8.1), and the launcher tells you if you need it. Both install over 0.3, and your save and settings stay

added Frame generation: makes an extra frame after each real one, so the game shows 60 frames a second while running at 30. It looks smoother but with the latency of 30. You can set it to Off, On or Auto in the launcher or the in-game menu. Auto only turns it on when your phone can't hold 60 but can keep up with frame generation. The motion comes from the game's own camera and objects, so the extra frames line up well with the real ones. This ran pretty well for me but might be troublesome for older phones, so use Fast quality for it to run a bit better.

Frame generation also has a quality setting. High gives Mario, enemies and other moving objects their own motion. Fast follows only the camera and is meant for slower GPUs

releases.name: beta 3.0
releases.body:
Beta 0.3

This update focuses on speed. On my Galaxy S24 Ultra (Snapdragon 8 Gen 3) Cascade now runs at about 58-60 fps, a pretty good improvement from about 44 in 0.2. On a tester’s Xiaomi with a Dimensity 8300 (Mali-G615) it runs at about 40 fps, fairly stable, with no graphical issues. Your results will likely be different, since it depends a lot on your phone.

What’s new:

Mali phones should see one of the biggest changes: the GPU doesnt sit idle waiting for the CPU anymore, so the game uses about 1 GB less memory now

A new “Preparing graphics” progress bar on game starts, instead of the frozen Joy-Con screen. (as always this will take a hot second if its your first launch, give it a minute to build the cache, and any launch after that should be MUCH faster.

the new Steady game speed:D, replacement of the original 30 fps option,now its  an option that keeps the game at normal speed at ANY fps below 60 fps. This means you can run the game at any fps and the game will NOT run in slow motion, as long as you enable it.
(its still recomended that you cap the fps to something you can consistantly hit)

releases.name: beta 0.2
releases.body:
the second release, big imrpvoement for the 60 fps mode, and Mali phones finally look right.

**Performance (my S24 Ultra, phone's own driver)**
- 60 fps mode: 60 fps in small and medium areas, 40-45ish in some heavy areas
- 30 fps mode: full speed, holds 30 most of the time

**What's new**
- Much better fps in the 60 fps mode in my tests, though the picture gets softer when the game lowers its render size
- Mali visual errors fixed on the one phone we've tested so far (thanks u/CAPELINI_W). Other Mali phones are untested
- New default settings on fresh installs. They run faster but make the phone warmer

**Updating from 0.1?** Install it over 0.1. Your old settings stay, so to get the speedup set these in Graphics: Presentation **Mailbox**, CPU boost **Always**, Custom scale **100%**, Anti-aliasing **FXAA**, Sharpening **75%**. The first start rebuilds the shaders, so expect one slow load.

You still need your own copy of the game (1.0.0) and `prod.keys`.

Thanks to u/zzzarathustra-dev ([Power Moon Recomp](https://gitlab.com/zzzarathustra-dev/power-moon-recomp)) and peiikai ([LAS Recomp](https://github.com/peiikai/LASRecomp)) for the findings and optimizations we borrowed.

releases.body:
## 核心变更

### 1. Flyme 12.6 / Android 16 反孤儿进程根治（`libsubreaper.so`）
- 经魅族 21 Note（Flyme 12.6 / Android 16）控制变量实测，系统会在 `< 100ms` 内静默终止普通应用 UID 下托孤给 `init`（`PPID=1`）的孤儿进程。
- 内置 368 字节纯静态 PIE（`ET_DYN`、64KB 对齐）AArch64 启动器 `lib/arm64-v8a/libsubreaper.so`，通过 `prctl(PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER, 1)` 接管整个 Wine 进程子树并循环 `wait4(-1)` 回收已退出子进程（含 `-EINTR` 重试，兼容暂停/恢复）。

releases.name: NDS Station per Android 2.2.0
releases.body:
## Novità per gli amministratori

- **Cambia nome utente**: dalla lista utenti. L'utente viene disconnesso e accede di nuovo con il nuovo nome; salvataggi, console e amici restano invariati.
- **Salvataggi di un giocatore**: per ogni gioco puoi scaricare il salvataggio del giocatore oppure sostituirlo (o crearlo) con un file .sav, anche esportato da DeSmuME o da un altro emulatore. Prima di caricare viene chiesta conferma, con un avviso se le dimensioni non corrispondono al salvataggio attuale. La versione sostituita resta nella cronologia del server, e se il giocatore stava giocando su quella vecchia all'uscita gli viene chiesto quale tenere.

## Altre modifiche

- I dati locali (ROM in cache, copie dei salvataggi, stati salvati) sono legati all'account e non più al nome utente: dopo un cambio di nome restano al loro posto. Alla prima apertura vengono spostati automaticamente.

## Requisiti

Server [nds-server-emulator-fastapi](https://github.com/federico-castellani/nds-server-emulator-fastapi) aggiornato (commit `7d2701c`). Con un server precedente l'app funziona, ma le nuove funzioni di amministrazione non sono disponibili.

releases.name: NDS Station per Android 2.0.1
releases.body:
Prima versione per Android di NDS Station, con le stesse funzioni del client Windows 2.0.1.

- Libreria del server con ricerca; ROM scaricate e tenute in cache.
- Emulatore melonDS con tasti virtuali su schermo, touch sullo schermo inferiore, controller fisici, pausa, avanti veloce e stati salvati.

Scarica `NDSStation-2.0.1.apk` sul telefono e aprilo (va consentita l'installazione da origini sconosciute). L'APK è firmato con una chiave di sviluppo: per aggiornarlo in futuro usa sempre gli APK di queste release.

releases.body:
Windows, Linux (x86_64 and ARM64), macOS (Apple Silicon) and Android (arm64).

## What changed since 2.2.0

Bug reports sent from msr2ds itself, Discord Rich Presence, and fixes for Arachnus, the Teleport Station and 30 FPS.

- **Send a bug report from msr2ds.** The new **REPORT** tab, in the launcher and in the game's F1 menu, sends your report to GitHub Issues with the log of the play session you choose. In the game, the session you're playing comes first. You sign in to GitHub with a code the tab shows you (a free account is enough), and the report goes up under your name, so you see the replies.
- **Discord Rich Presence.** With the Discord app open on the same computer, your profile shows that you're playing msr2ds, the area you're in, the Metroids left and the time played. The **Discord Rich Presence** switch on the Game tab turns it off. Not in the Android app.
- **Join the msr2ds Discord** from the Game tab, in the launcher or in the game.
- **Arachnus no longer sinks into the floor** above 30 FPS. At 120 and 144 FPS, its roll in the Area 2 arena lost the floor, and it sank into the rock.

releases.name: msr2ds 2.2.0
releases.body:
Windows, Linux (x86_64 and ARM64), macOS (Apple Silicon) and Android (arm64).

## What changed since 2.1.0

Stereoscopic 3D, nothing missing in wide views anymore, and a log for every play session.

- **Stereoscopic 3D** (#17). Side by side, for 3D TVs, Acer SpatialLabs displays and VR headsets. The game draws both eyes itself, as on a 3DS. On the Display tab: **Stereoscopic 3D** (side by side at half width or at full width), **3D depth** (the 3DS's 3D slider, 10-100%) and **Swap eyes**. It needs the Vulkan renderer.
- **Nothing missing in wide views.** In 16:9 and ultrawide, some breakable blocks and pieces of rock were not drawn. The game draws at most 300 level pieces at a time, and a wider view holds more than that. Now every piece in view is drawn.
- **The game's message boxes keep their shape.** "Save your progress?", "Use the Teleport Station?" and the other boxes the game shows over play no longer stretch in 16:9 and ultrawide.

releases.name: msr2ds 2.1.0
releases.body:
Windows, Linux (x86_64 and ARM64), macOS (Apple Silicon) and Android (arm64).

## What changed since 2.0.9

A fix for the Android phones that crashed at the title screen in 2.0.9, and a pause screen redone for controllers and wide screens.

- **Android: no more crash at the title screen on Adreno 830 phones** (#58, #37). On Snapdragon 8 Elite devices (the Odin 3 and phones with the same chip), 2.0.9 crashed at the first 3D scene: the graphics driver's shader compiler crashed building 2.0.9's new per-material lighting. On Adreno GPUs, lighting now works as it did in 2.0.8, and the lighting code is back in the shape their compiler handled. Other GPUs keep 2.0.9's faster lighting. If 2.0.9 left the app in its safe graphics mode after a crash, this update clears it.
- **The pause screen fills the window**, now on by default (HUD tab: **Fit the pause screen to the window**). Its bars and background reach the window's edges, its buttons and text keep their shape, and the map fills the width, so you see more of the area.

releases.name: msr2ds 2.0.9
releases.body:
Windows, Linux (x86_64 and ARM64), macOS (Apple Silicon) and Android (arm64).

## What changed since 2.0.8

Mostly Android fixes, and faster lighting everywhere.

- **Android: "Not built yet" with the native code in place** (#58, #63). On some devices (an Odin 3 in #58), Android gives a `recomp-android` folder copied in from a PC an owner the app can't read. The app now makes the `recomp-android` folder itself, so a copy from the PC goes into a folder it owns. If a folder you copied in earlier can't be read, the launcher says so and what to do: delete that folder from the PC, then copy the two files from the PC's `recomp-android` folder (`libmsr_aot.so` and `module.json`) into the empty one the app makes in its place. A copy dropped inside the app's folder (`recomp-android/recomp-android`) is moved up. `launcher.log` says what the launcher found.

releases.body:
## Type your own name

Until now a new game was always named "Flip", because the console's on-screen keyboard did nothing in the port. Now, when you start a new game, a text box with Android's keyboard asks for your name:

- **✓** on the keyboard (or **OK**) accepts. **Back** cancels and returns to the save slot list.
- Like on the original console, an empty name, a name made only of spaces, or the characters the game does not allow (space, @, %, / and \) open the box again with the reason.
- An empty file `sin_teclado` in the game folder brings back the old behaviour.

Nothing else changes: graphics, frame rate and shader caches are the same as in 1.4.0.

## Installing

Install the APK over the previous version (your settings and saves stay) or follow the [README](https://github.com/IamWilmar/nier-recomp#install-and-first-run) for a first install.

releases.name: NieR:Automata port v1.4.0
releases.body:
## Save report and update notices

Two new rows in the settings panel (swipe in from the right edge of the screen):

- **Save report** writes a folder `reports/<date>/` into your game folder: the log, a screenshot of the moment you opened the panel, the frame times of the last seconds and basic device information (model, Android version, memory). **Nothing is sent anywhere.** If something looks wrong, open an [issue](https://github.com/IamWilmar/nier-recomp/issues) and attach those files (have a look first: the log contains the names of your folders).
- **Update notices** (on by default): about eight seconds after the game starts, the app asks GitHub's public API which release is the latest. It is a single request, without an account, and nothing about you or your game is sent. If there is a newer version, a banner says so and *Get vX.Y.Z* opens its page. Switch it off in the panel (or create an empty file `sin_avisos_version` in the game folder) and the app makes no network request at all.
- Because of the update notices the app now has Android's **Internet** permission. It is used for that request only.

## Installing

- **Bluetooth and USB controllers fixed.** The Retroid's system re-creates every external controller with the device's own IDs, so the port took a DualSense (or any other pad) for the built-in one and, in Retro mode, swapped its buttons. releases.name: Pokemon Legends Arceus V1.2
releases.body:
## Arceus Recomp for Android – Update

### Highlights
- **Game code is now built on your phone.** The APK no longer ships any game code. After you pick your own `prod.keys`, game (`.nsp`/`.xci`) and update in **Game Files**, the app translates and compiles `libgame.so` on the device using a bundled Python, translator, clang and lld. It takes about 10 minutes on an Odin 3, and if it's interrupted it picks up where it left off. When it finishes, **Play** appears and you can delete the game files from your phone.
- **Music and voices work.** The Switch's Opus decoder service (hwopus) is now implemented with libopus 1.5.2.

### Better support for other phones
- **Automatic performance profiles.** On first start the app picks a profile from your GPU (Adreno, Mali/Immortalis, Xclipse, PowerVR) and your RAM. You can change it under *Video > Android > Performance profile*.
  - **High:** 100% resolution, 60 fps (Snapdragon 8 Gen 2 and newer).
  - **Medium:** dynamic resolution (never below 60%), 60 fps.
  - **Light:** 75% resolution, 30 fps, half-size shadows.

releases.name: Pokemon Legends Arceus Android First Release
releases.body:
# Arceus Recomp for Android — v1.0 

Android port of **PokeL-ARecomp**, the static recompilation of *Pokémon Legends: Arceus*. Tested on the AYN Odin 3 (Snapdragon 8 Elite, Adreno 830).

> ⚠️ This repository **does not include the game, keys or game code**. Every player uses their own legal copy.

## ✨ What's new

### Performance and heat
- **60 fps at 60 Hz with 100% resolution.**
- **Much less heat:** CPU went from ~84 °C to ~52 °C and the fan is barely audible.
- **CPU cores:** the game uses 4 cores and leaves the rest free. You can pick All / 4 / 2.
- **Clock speeds:** the port tells Android how long each frame really takes, on the CPU and the GPU. The CPU no longer sits at max clock, and the GPU clocks up when it needs to.
- **Less data copying:** GPU constants are read straight from shared memory, so about 80% less data is copied per frame.
- **Pause in the background:** the game pauses when you leave the app.

### Graphics
- **Vulkan on Adreno**, with support for the **Turnip** (Mesa) driver, which you can import and pick from the menu.
- **"Soft" anti-aliasing** (new, default): blends the dithered pattern on hair, leaves and grass at no fps cost. SMAA is also available.

## BluBox 360 macOS 3.0.2 Preview

This Mac preview fixes the update experience and keeps the 3.0.1 Xenia launch hotfix.

- Adds **BluBox 360 > Software Update…** inside the app.
- Shows your installed version, the latest available Mac version, status, and release notes.
- Shows an in-app update banner when a newer Mac preview is available.
- Checks for a newer Mac preview automatically after launch.
- Adds **Update Now** for future Mac updates.
- Downloads the Mac ZIP from GitHub Releases and verifies it against `SHA256SUMS.txt` before installing.
- Replaces the existing app in place when macOS permits it, so the older version does not need to be uninstalled first.
- If macOS requires extra permission, BluBox opens the DMG so you can drag the new app over the old one and choose **Replace** instead of uninstalling.

**Preview warning:** this remains experimental macOS emulator software. CI verifies the app, bundled engines, launch sanitizer, signatures, update payload checksums, and startup self-tests. It does not prove that every Xbox 360 game boots or runs correctly.

releases.body:
# BluBox 360 0.16.3 public alpha

BluBox 360 0.16.3 focuses on easier updating and safer sustained performance on Android handhelds such as the AYN Thor.

## Check for updates

- Added a **Check for updates** button under **Settings > App**.
- Automatic update checks keep the existing 15-minute cooldown.
- A manual check runs immediately and ignores the automatic cooldown.
- Manual checks now confirm when BluBox is already up to date.
- Manual checks show an error message if GitHub cannot be reached instead of silently closing.

## Smart Heat Guard

- Low Heat Mode remains available and still avoids maximum-clock requests.
- BluBox now checks Android thermal status and thermal headroom when a game launches.
- When Android reports thermal pressure, BluBox uses the low-heat launch preset even if Low Heat Mode was switched off.
- A 60 FPS target can be reduced to a 30 FPS safety ceiling when the device is already approaching thermal throttling.
- Shader creation is reduced to one worker under thermal pressure to lower sustained CPU load.
- Fable II keeps its existing 24 FPS safety ceiling.
- The existing severe-heat protection remains enabled during gameplay.

- Mali GPUs: geometry no longer explodes into streaks on Mali GPUs (Exynos, Dimensity, Tensor, Kirin), which lack the clip-distance feature.

## Performance
- Each thread keeps its own cache of recently freed small blocks and reuses them without taking the global heap lock. In testing, an allocate-and-free went from about 34 ms to 5 ms. Freeing the same block twice is still detected and logged though.
- A thread that re-enters a lock it already holds now just counts up the way Windows does, instead of going through the real lock each time.
- Memory copies: the base memcpy routine, about 10% of all CPU, now runs as Android's native copy.
- The game reads the clock hundreds of thousands of times a second. QueryPerformanceCounter, GetTickCount and timeGetTime now read the processor's hardware timer instead of making a system call.
- A missing Data folder is now remembered after the first check - no repeated path search and log line each time.

# WinLite v1.4.0

## Overview
A release focused on rendering smoothness, a new X11 server and Steam support.

---

## 🎮 BETA - Steam
- Steam client support added.

---

## 🖥️ X11 server (rewritten in Rust)
The built-in X server has been rewritten from scratch in Rust and now covers much more of the X11 protocol.

**What you get**
- **Stability.** Memory-safe code removes a whole class of crashes and hangs.
- **Better game and launcher compatibility.** Newer screen-configuration (RANDR 1.2) and rendering extensions are supported, so Wine, launchers and games see a more complete environment.
- **Proper mouse cursors.** System cursors are drawn from a built-in cursor set, and colored/semi-transparent and animated cursors are supported.
- **Better frame pacing.** Frame presentation is synchronized with the real display refresh rate and with fences, which gives the renderer and the FPS limiter an accurate clock to work from.
- **Faster window drawing.** The shared frame buffer is locked once per operation instead of repeatedly, and more drawing requests (lines, rectangles, area clears) are handled directly.

> [!IMPORTANT]

What's new in v2.3
This release is about speed and game compatibility. The emulation changes are listed here so you know what touches the game itself.
CPU boost and GPU boost (Settings > General > Performance). CPU boost runs the game's SSE math on your PC's processor and trims work in the CPU emulation. Per-game settings and safe mode. Each game can have its own CPU boost, GPU boost and shader seeding, used the next time it starts (Settings > General > Performance > This game). releases.body:
天玑 / MediaTek X11 专版 · 合成器测试版

本版基于 1.2.0 天玑 X11 分支，**唯一改动是打开 KWin 合成器**，用于真机验证桌面特效（窗口晃动、魔灯等）能否真正生效。

#### 本版改了什么

此前每次启动桌面会话时，脚本都会把 `kwinrc` 强制改写为：

```ini
[Compositing]
Enabled=false
Backend=QPainter
```

这正是「在系统设置里勾了窗口晃动 / 魔灯，晃了半天毫无反应」的直接原因——**合成器关着，KWin 会静默忽略全部桌面特效**。

本版改为：

```ini
[Compositing]
Enabled=true
Backend=OpenGL
GLCore=false
LatencyPolicy=Low
WindowsBlockCompositing=false
```

后端固定为 **OpenGL（硬件）**，不使用纯软件 QPainter 后端；LLVM 软件渲染（llvmpipe / swrast）在部署时仍会被删除。

#### ⚠️ 这是未经验证的测试版，请只用于测试

发布者手上没有天玑真机，**本版没有在任何天玑设备上跑过**。请把预期放低。

已知的关键疑点（在我的机器上实测发现，属于**设备无关**的问题）：

1. **guest rootfs 内缺少 `virpipe_dri.so`**。逐个列出 rootfs 中全部 Mesa DRI 驱动后确认：有 `virtio_gpu_dri.so`、`zink_dri.so`、`panfrost_dri.so`、`mediatek_dri.so`，**但没有 `virpipe_dri.so`**——而这正是 VirGL 的 guest 端驱动。会话脚本仍在强制 `GALLIUM_DRIVER=virpipe` + `VTEST_SOCKET=/tmp/.virgl_test`，即**指向一个不存在的驱动**。若真机因此拿不到 GL 上下文，合成器就起不来。
2. **相反方向的证据**：发布者在高通测试机上开启 OpenGL 合成后桌面全黑，日志为 `MESA: error: ZINK: vkGetCalibratedTimestampsEXT failed (VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_HOST_MEMORY)`。但那条日志同时说明 **KWin 当时确实拿到了 GL 上下文**（走的是 Zink）。这与第 1 点互相矛盾，怀疑 KWin 走 EGL 入口、Qt 走 GLX 入口，两者对 `GALLIUM_DRIVER` 的处理不同。

## Changes

- **Lower CPU use during races on Android.** A check the game makes very often (whenever two game threads coordinate) now skips work it had already done, so races need less of the phone's CPU. This is aimed at slower phones such as the Pixel 10a, where the CPU is the limit. On the AYN Thor the game used about 15–20% less CPU time in the middle of a race. The picture and the race are unchanged. For #176

## Validation

- **CPU time on the AYN Thor** (the middle of a Dolphin Resort race, CPU seconds the game used per second): 1.81 against 2.19 in 0.10.76 for a normal race, 1.78 against 2.18 with touch and tilt, 1.81 against 2.18 with camera motion, 2.51 against 3.15 at Race step rate 120, 1.87 against 2.20 with CPU difficulty Hard.
- **The rest, as in 0.10.76:**
  - **Windows x64 package:**
    - A whole Dolphin Resort race on Vulkan with the validation layer: no errors, full speed (1.000).
    - The title movie, Sharp scaling and an Avatar award in the middle of a race.
    - Direct3D 11 (experimental) at feature levels 11.1 and 11.0.
    - The copy without AVX: full speed, and no AVX instructions outside Microsoft's C runtime.

## Changes

- **Less CPU time spent drawing each race frame.** The game's main thread now finds textures and sets them up for drawing with much less work, so busy frames with many objects on screen are less likely to run late, especially on phones that slow down when they get hot. On the AYN Thor, drawing a race frame takes about 0.7 ms less (about a fifth less per object drawn). The picture is unchanged. For #176

## Validation

- **Drawing time on the AYN Thor** (frame timing on, the middle of a Dolphin Resort race): 2.8 ms of drawing a frame and 3.1 µs per object, against 3.4–3.7 ms and 4.0–4.1 µs in 0.10.75; texture work went from about 1.0 ms to 0.3 ms a frame.
- **The picture is unchanged on Windows:** the same Windows checks as 0.10.75 all passed (see below), and while PR #454 was tested, the new code drew the same 27 pictures bit for bit as 0.10.75 from the title screen up to the race (races themselves never repeat exactly, so they were compared by eye).
- **The rest, as in 0.10.75:**
  - **Windows x64 package:**
    - A whole Dolphin Resort race on Vulkan with the validation layer: no errors, full speed (1.000).
